ticket.title: feature request ✨
ticket.description:
#### Customer Email

<email>

#### Workspace name

AI Acquisition Sales Team

#### Workspace ID

<uuid>

#### Which lead?

none

#### What's wrong?

please can you add the prospects timing that the call will be. see in the screenshot it says 2pm, which is my time in the UK, when i call the prospect its essential i tell them their call is at, for example, 9am (in their timezone: eastern, central, pacific).

would be super helpful if the time their call was could be visible in their timezone as well as my own

#### Screenshot

 <image> 

#### Video link

#### Scope

The meeting cards on the contact and deal Meetings tabs label the rep's time with their timezone and add the prospect's time, using the timezone the prospect booked in. The contact's timezone is not used as a fallback.

Done when:

* A UK rep sees their time labelled BST/GMT and the prospect's Eastern time on a Calendly booking.
* No prospect time appears for a booking stored as UTC, or when the rep and prospect share the same clock.
* It works on both the contact and deal Meetings tabs.

relatedSnapshot.title: Feature request: GoHighLevel (Lead Connector) integration and dynamic Name 1 Meet links
relatedSnapshot.description:
Feature request from an Intercom conversation with a customer whose primary CRM is GoHighLevel (GHL) and who runs AI SDR campaigns.

Two related asks:

1. GoHighLevel (Lead Connector) integration
   The customer wants leads qualified in Acquisity to sync natively into GHL. Today there is no native GHL sync; the working path is a manual CSV export from the CRM (People, Companies, Deals, and Appointments each export separately) and import into GHL. A public CRM API and a Zapier bridge are on the roadmap but not yet available.
2. Dynamic Name 1 Meet links
   The customer wants the AI SDR to use a dynamic Name 1 Meet link (a unique link per booking). Today Conferencing supports only a static meeting link or dynamic Zoom links.

relatedSnapshot.title: Allow lead scraper preview before spending credits
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Feature Request

User requested a way to spot check lead lists generated by the lead scraper before credits are consumed.

They reported setting what they believed were the correct filters, but the resulting list did not match the intended target audience. This used 2,500 credits on an unusable list. The request is to be able to review at least an initial subset of leads (e.g. first 100) prior to purchase so incorrect lists do not result in wasted spend.

This is a feature request, not a bug report.

relatedSnapshot.title: Make message status filter support multi-select
relatedSnapshot.description:
user: <email>

The "filter by" dropdown at the top of the messages section should support selecting multiple statuses.

Current behavior makes it hard to exclude out-of-office replies while still viewing conversations with other statuses, including messages that have no status beyond "New". The request is to allow viewing all statuses except out of office.

This affects workflow every day because out-of-office replies are considered distracting and not relevant.

---

## Problem Statement

The "Filter by" status dropdown at the top of the AI SDR inbox is single-select, so users cannot view conversations across multiple statuses at once. Customers asked for the ability to view all statuses except out-of-office, since OOO replies are noisy.

## Impact Analysis

* **User Impact**: Daily friction for customers who want to triage replies while filtering out OOO. They had to repeatedly switch the status filter or manually scroll past OOO threads.
* **Development Impact**: None — the existing single-select code paths required minor refactoring to support arrays without changing single-status behavior.
* **Business Impact**: Improves the inbox triage experience for AI SDR users, reducing time-to-reply on real conversations.

## Root Cause

`statusFilter` was modeled as a single string everywhere — UI dropdown, URL state (`nuqs` `parseAsString`), `useAiSdrEmails` hook, the `outreach.leads.getOrganizationEmailActivities` tRPC input, and the `getStatusCondition` / `getStatusConditionDrizzle` repository helpers — so only one status could ever be active.

## Solution Overview

Threaded `string | string[]` through every layer and converted the dropdown to a checkbox-style multi-select.

* `components/ai-sdr/email-list.tsx`: `DropdownMenuItem` → `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem`. Each option toggles membership in the array; "Clear filters" resets it. Trigger label shows "All Statuses" when empty, the single label when one is picked, and "N statuses" when multiple are picked.
* `components/ai-sdr/ai-sdr-inbox.tsx`: URL state uses `parseAsArrayOf(parseAsString).withDefault([])` so multi-select selections survive reloads/back-forward. Status array is forwarded to `useAiSdrEmails`, the sample-mode filter, and reset (`[]`) when leaving sample mode.
* `hooks/use-ai-sdr-emails.tsx`: accepts `StatusFilterValue | StatusFilterValue[] | string | string[]` and forwards the value (or the sidebar `selectedGroup` fallback) to the tRPC query.
* `trpc/routers/outreach/leads.ts`: introduces `statusFilterValueSchema` (an enum of all known statuses) and accepts `z.union([statusFilterValueSchema, z.array(statusFilterValueSchema).max(15)])` so callers must send a known status and the array length is bounded (addresses Codex's DOS/abuse concern).
* `lib/outreach/db/campaign.ts`: split each per-status condition out of `getStatusCondition` (raw SQL) and `getStatusConditionDrizzle` (Drizzle, used for the count query) into a `buildSingleStatusCondition*` helper, then `OR` them together when an array is supplied. Single-string callers behave exactly as before. A shared `normalizeStatusFilters` helper coerces input to a clean string array.
* `components/ai-sdr/sample-data/constants.ts`: `filterSampleSdrEmails` accepts `string | string[]` and matches with `Array.some(matchesGroup)`.

## How to QA

1. Sign in as a user with the AI SDR Inbox enabled and visit `/dashboard/<org>/ai-sdr`.
2. Click the **Filter by** dropdown at the top of the inbox list. Verify it now shows checkboxes (Interested, Meeting Booked, Not Interested, Out of Office, Do Not Contact) and a "Clear filters" item appears once any are checked.
3. Tick **Interested** and **Meeting Booked**. Confirm:
   * The trigger label reads "2 statuses".
   * The list updates to threads matching either status (OR semantics), with no out-of-office threads mixed in.
   * The URL contains `?status=interested,booked` (comma-separated).
   * Reloading the page restores the same selection.
4. Untick everything (or click **Clear filters**). Confirm the trigger reads "All Statuses" and the unfiltered inbox returns.
5. Tick only **Out of Office** and verify only OOO threads appear.
6. Combine with the sidebar groups (e.g. "Needs Attention") and the campaign + search filters — they should compose with the multi-select instead of replacing it.
7. Switch to the sample data demo and repeat steps 2–4 — sample data should respect the same filter semantics.
8. Verify nothing regressed for single-status callers: a stale URL like `?status=interested` (single value) should still load and behave the same as before.

## Visual changes

E2E walkthrough recorded against the Vercel preview using sample inbox data (8 sample emails).

**Video walkthrough:** multi-select-e2e-edited.mp4

**1. Dropdown renders 5 status options as checkboxes (**`All Statuses`, 8/8 emails):

 <image> 

**2. Selecting Interested + Meeting Booked → URL** `?status=interested,booked`, label `2 statuses`, 5 emails (OR semantics):

 <image> 

**3.** Loading `?status=interested,booked,attention` directly → label `3 statuses` (URL hydration verified).

**4.** Single-status URL `?status=booked` → label `Meeting Booked` (backward compatibility verified).

**5. "Clear filters" → URL clean, label** `All Statuses`, 8/8 emails restored:

 <image> 

## Additional Context

* Backwards-compatible: existing `?status=<single>` URLs and any external callers that still pass a single string keep working — the repository helpers detect single vs. array and emit the same SQL as before for the single case.
* Bot review: Codex's "constrain unbounded array" P2 finding was addressed in commit `157ae0c` (`.max(15)` + enum validation). Cubic AI confirmed all six acceptance criteria; Name 10 Review found no bugs.

## Related

* PR: <url:github.com>

relatedSnapshot.title: Feature request: Allow creating custom folders in the AI SDR Inbox
relatedSnapshot.description:
Customer feature request from an Intercom conversation.

**Source: **<url:app.intercom.com>

**Request:** Allow users to create custom folders in the AI SDR Inbox to organize threads, for example one folder per company they work with.

**Customer's words:** "My second feature request is to have the ability to create folders in my inbox. I want to make folders for each company I work with. Right now it's just a jumbled mess in my inbox."

**Current behavior:** The AI SDR Inbox has a fixed folder structure. Top folders are Inbox, Needs Attention, AI SDR Disabled, and Name 13; collapsible sections are All Campaigns, Responses (Interested / Not Interested / Meeting Booked), and Others (Out of Office / Bounced / Unsubscribed). There is no way to create custom folders.

**Proposed:** Let users create and name their own folders in the inbox and move or tag threads into them for organization.
